item.title: HiRO-ACEv2: Simulating extreme weather at 3 km resolution for a fraction of the cost
item.description: HiRO-ACEv2 captures extreme rain, wind, and pressure events at 3 km resolution for about 1/300th the cost of X-SHiELD, making detailed global climate simulations more accessible to researchers.

item.title: How Molmo 2’s open release helped an MIT researcher rethink fish tracking
item.description: Molmo 2’s open release helped MIT researcher Kai Van Brunt develop Molmo2Fish, an experimental model that tracks salmon in sonar footage and corrects some tracking errors using everyday language.

item.title: Impactful scheduling for GPU clusters
item.description: We explain how Ai2’s new GPU scheduler uses time budgets, fair-share allocation, and time-slicing to prioritize high-impact research, shorten queue waits, and keep GPUs busy.

item.title: Ai2 at COLM 2026: Open research, from models to agents for science
item.description: Ai2 joined COLM 2026 to share advances in open language models, training infrastructure, and AI for science, including Olmo Hybrid, Asta, and Bolmo, while connecting with the broader research community.

item.title: Now in Nature: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes
item.description: The technique behind Bolmo, Ai2’s fully open byte-level language models, is now published in Nature, with new checkpoints showing the approach generalizes beyond Olmo to other model families.

item.title: Open-sourcing AstaBrief, the fast report-generation model in Asta
item.description: We’re releasing AstaBrief, an 8B open-weights model for generating cited scientific reports, available in Asta’s Fast mode or to download and run on your own infrastructure.

item.title: Introducing Olmo-core 3: Open, scalable training infrastructure for large MoEs
item.description: Olmo-core 3 introduces a redesigned, fully open training stack for efficiently scaling mixture-of-experts models into the trillion-parameter range.

item.title: What a crowdsourced game revealed about steering Olmo 3
item.description: A crowdsourced game built on Olmo 3 showed how people can exploit unexpected model behaviors to stress-test prosocial AI evaluations—and how open access to a model’s internals can help researchers understand why those tests break.
